result:
The answer 10 is incorrect, because the claim that A₅ is the only group in 𝒢 is false.

Consider PSL(2,8). Its nonlinear irreducible character degrees are 7, 8 and 9. Each of these is a prime power (7, 2³ and 3²), so each has exactly one distinct prime divisor. PSL(2,8) is non-solvable, so it lies in 𝒢. The prime 7 divides the degree 7 and is not in {2, 3, 5}, so 7 ∈ P. This shows P ≠ {2, 3, 5}.

The proposed solution relies on an unjustified "it is known" claim that A₅ is unique, and that claim fails.

VERDICT: REJECT
